hero.accessibleHeadline: A team and a memory for OpenCode
hero.support: Hivemind is two plugins for OpenCode V2. Steward runs Devin, Antigravity and Freebuff inside your session, as the agent you talk to or as delegates. Substrate keeps an exact record of everything they did.

intro.text: remembers every session, child and diff, on your own disk.

tabs.title: Three agents, one terminal
tabs.body: Open Devin, Antigravity or Freebuff as a real session in the OpenCode terminal and watch it work, or let your agent delegate to any of them and keep going. Pick any model each one offers.

tabs.title: Keep an exact memory
tabs.body: Archive every session tree into your project, index who did what, prune stale tool output without losing the facts, and trace any change back to the session and subagent that made it.

items.name: Install it
items.body: One command per plugin, for every project or just this one.

items.name: Reload OpenCode
items.body: Plugins load at startup, so restart once after installing.

items.name: Set up once, then forget it
items.body: /hivemind-setup asks which harnesses and models to use, saves the answers and stays out of the way.

install.body: Copy the commands for your setup. Nothing installs itself: OpenCode picks the plugins up the next time it starts.

notes.stewardProject: Add this entry to the plugins array in this project's opencode.json.
notes.substrateProject: Adds Substrate to ./opencode.json, keeping your comments.
notes.setup: In OpenCode, run this once and answer the questions.

hero.accessibleHeadline: Devin, Antigravity and Freebuff, inside OpenCode
hero.support: Open Devin, Antigravity or Freebuff as a real session in your OpenCode terminal when you want to watch. Hand any of them a task in the background when you don't.
hero.installNote: Latest on npm: 0.4.0. Needs OpenCode 2.1.2 or later, below v3.

items.sentence: Watch them work in your terminal.
items.consequence: /devin, /antigravity or /freebuff opens a real session: streaming replies, file mentions and a model picker.

items.sentence: Hand off a task and keep going.
items.consequence: hivemind-delegate runs it in a genuine child session on Devin, Antigravity or Freebuff. Foreground waits for the result; background returns now and reports later.
Requests show up as cards with the agent's own options. Auto-approve on delegated sessions is off unless you turn it on.

items.sentence: Pick up where a crash left off.
items.consequence: Each child records its binding. Recovery reloads the same foreign session and checks the replay, so your prompt is never sent twice.
Models come from each agent's live catalog, so new ones show up without a plugin update. Pick one per agent in /hivemind-setup or switch with ctrl+m.

try.heading: Try a command
try.sideTitle: Watch it, or hand it off.
try.sideBody: Open a session when you want to see the work and answer its questions. Delegate when you don't: the task runs in a real OpenCode child session and the result comes back to your agent.

setup.heading: Set up once.
setup.body: Run /hivemind-setup. If your saved setup is healthy it stops right away: no questions, no writes. If something is missing, your agent asks one question at a time and saves the answers.

steps.what: Choose which agents to enable, their fallback order, and a model for each.
One static read: ready, action-required or blocked, plus the one next thing to do.
Goes further only when you ask: a handshake by default, a session check with consent, install and sign-in after approval.

needs: OpenCode V2, version 2.1.2 or later, below v3.
For Devin: the devin CLI, signed in with devin auth login.
For Antigravity: the official Antigravity ACP server. The plugin can install the pinned build after you approve.
For Freebuff: your existing Freebuff login, or CODEBUFF_API_KEY in your environment.
setup.needsNote: The plugin checks for these. It never installs anything or signs you in on its own, and its settings accept no credentials.

closing.body: Cursor follows. Each ships only when both hosted sessions and delegation work. Your support pays for the hours.

hero.accessibleHeadline: Nothing your agent did goes missing
hero.support: Substrate archives every OpenCode session tree into your project, indexes it, and gives your agent two calls to find out exactly what changed and who changed it.
hero.installNote: Beta. Adds Substrate to your global OpenCode config, then reload OpenCode.

intro.text: indexes who did what. The valve clears old tool output and keeps the facts.

tabs.title: Every transcript, on disk
tabs.body: Each session tree, the root plus every subagent, delegate-devin and hivemind-delegate child, lands in .session-archive/ as JSONL. Long text goes to blobs named by their SHA-256, so nothing is stored twice. Running it again on unchanged sessions writes nothing.

tabs.title: Who did what, queryable
tabs.body: index.sqlite records sessions, delegations and their harness, file touches, test and build receipts, and a map of your code: AST skeletons, a PageRank repo map, and the files that change together in git.

tabs.title: Prune noise, keep the facts
tabs.body: substrate.valve swaps older tool output for breadcrumbs that point to the stored blob, and keeps a manifest of what is FRESH, SLICE or STALE. After compaction the agent picks up from the index instead of re-reading everything.

trace.heading: Two calls to the truth.
trace.body: When the agent goes idle, Substrate posts one line per change-set. The first call returns the package: branches ranked by what matters, in 800 tokens or fewer. The second opens a leaf: the diff with SHA-256 proof, the subagents that touched it, or which test results are now stale.
trace.demoNote: Sample data. In your project it comes from git and OpenCode's tool ledger.
trace.pickBranch: Pick a branch to open its leaf.

items.consequence: opencode.db is opened read-only. The archive lives in .session-archive/ at your project root, outside .opencode/.

items.sentence: Keeps the per-step hook in memory.
items.consequence: The context hook runs on every model step, so it does no disk work. It is built to a 2 ms budget, checked in tests.
Git history tells the agent which files usually change with the one it is editing, before it forgets one.
A compaction hook writes a continuity packet from the index, so the agent knows what was done and what is still open.

rows.what: Sync the archive and code index
Build a brief for a child agent
trace, search, repomap, skeleton, slice, coupled, brief, timeline

closing.body: Owner testing is still running. If something breaks, open an issue and include your OpenCode version: Substrate reads OpenCode's own data.
closing.privacy: Transcripts can hold anything pasted into a session. Treat .session-archive/ like a secret and decide yourself whether to commit it.
